title: Best Software for a New Dojo (2026): Startup Costs
description: Starting a martial arts school? Software costs compared at 0-50 students: free plans, $40-$79 flat tools, fees, trials and contracts, plus a checklist.
h1: Best software for a new dojo: startup costs and checklist
keyword: software for new martial arts school
body:
Opening a new martial arts school or BJJ academy means buying software before you have many students. On day one you mostly need four things: a way for people to book a free trial class, a signed waiver, automatic monthly billing, and a check-in list so you know who's training. Belt tracking, marketing automation and a branded app can wait. This guide compares what each school software vendor publishes about cost at the size most new schools start at: 0 to 50 students.

We checked each vendor's own pricing page on November 18, 2026. We haven't used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. Prices are in US dollars.

A worked example: 20 students at $150 a month

Say you open with 20 students paying $150 a month by card. That's $3,000 a month in tuition and 20 card payments. Here is what the published software and platform fees come to. For the Stripe-based tools, Stripe's own card fee comes on top and isn't included.

  • MatGoat Professional: $60/mo, no MatGoat fee. (Basic at $40 has no payment management, so you'd bill students another way.)
  • RhinoFit: $3,000 is over the $2,500 Start Up limit, so it's Standard at $57/mo, plus processing at rates RhinoFit doesn't publish.
  • MatPilot Free: $0 + 2% = $60/mo. MatPilot Pro: $79 + 0.49% ($14.70) = $93.70/mo. Pro becomes cheaper once you take about $5,230 a month through MatPilot.
  • Martialytics: $69/mo, no added fee.
  • MAAT: $59 + 1% ($30) = $89/mo.
  • Gymdesk: $75/mo with Gymdesk Payments, but its processing rate isn't published.
  • PushPress Free: $0, but the card rate is all-in at 4.99% + $0.30, which is $155.70/mo on $3,000. Pro is $159/mo plus 2.89% + $0.30 ($92.70), so $251.70/mo. Pro only costs less than Free above about $7,570 a month in card payments.
  • Kicksite: $49/mo for 0-25 students, plus Basys at $29/mo + 2.9% + $0.25 ($92), so $170/mo all-in with processing.
  • Zen Planner: $99/mo plus processing at unpublished rates.
  • Spark Membership: free for 8 weeks, then $199/mo plus Spark Payments at unpublished rates.

The all-in numbers for PushPress and Kicksite include card processing; the others don't, so add your processor's fee before comparing them. To run your own numbers, use our membership revenue calculator or see martial arts billing software for processing fees in more detail.

Startup checklist: what to set up before your first class

  1. Pick software well before you open. Zen Planner's FAQ recommends having its system ready 3-6 months ahead of launch. Whatever you choose, leave time to build your schedule, memberships and waiver before you start taking sign-ups.
  2. Start the free trial when you can actually use it. Trials run 7 days (MAAT), 30 days (Gymdesk, Martialytics, MatGoat, Kicksite, RhinoFit) or 8 weeks (Spark). MatPilot and PushPress have free plans, so there's no clock.
  3. Get a waiver signed at sign-up. RhinoFit lists RhinoSign digital waivers on every plan, including Start Up. For other tools, ask whether waivers are included and whether a parent can sign for a child (see kids martial arts software for family accounts and guardian waivers).
  4. Turn on autopay before the first billing date. On MatGoat, payment management is on Professional only. RhinoFit lists Automated Payment Processing and email/SMS on Standard; the Start Up plan may restrict payment processing and communications.
  5. Set up trial-class booking on your website. Gymdesk includes a gym website on every plan. MatPilot adds a website for +$25/mo on Pro, RhinoFit sells a custom website and hosting for $25/mo, and Zen Planner's website starts at $99/mo. Compare them in martial arts software with a website included.
  6. Plan for the first price step. Several tools price by active students, so your bill rises as you grow: Kicksite goes from $49 to $99/mo at 26 students, Zen Planner from $99 to $133/mo at 46, Martialytics from $69 to $99/mo at 51, and Gymdesk from $75 to $100/mo at 51 (with Gymdesk Payments). MatGoat Basic stops at 50 students. Flat-price tools (MatPilot Pro, MAAT, MatGoat Professional, RhinoFit Standard, PushPress) don't change with headcount.
  7. Read the contract before you sign. Spark's terms set your service term in an Order Form and auto-renew it unless you give 30 days' notice. Kicksite's annual plans auto-renew and aren't refunded if cancelled early. Gymdesk, MatPilot, MatGoat, Martialytics, RhinoFit, MAAT (monthly) and Zen Planner say they're month to month or have no contract.
  8. Leave belt tracking and marketing for later if you need to. Most of these tools include belt or rank tracking (see belt rank tracking software), but marketing add-ons such as Zen Planner Engage ($249/mo) and branded apps (PushPress $97/mo, Gymdesk $100/mo, Zen Planner $39 or $99/mo depending on which of its pages you read) rarely make sense before you have students.

Which option fits which kind of new school

  • Garage gym or very small club (under 20 students, under $2,500 a month): RhinoFit Start Up ($0) or MatPilot Free ($0 + 2%) let you start without a monthly bill. Check what the RhinoFit free tier leaves out. {{aff:matpilot|See MatPilot pricing}}
  • Small BJJ academy that wants a low flat price: MatGoat Professional ($60/mo, no added fee) or MAAT ($59/mo or $49/mo annual, plus 1%). {{aff:matgoat|See MatGoat pricing}}
  • Traditional dojo planning to grow past 50 students: Martialytics ($69/mo, all features on every tier) or Gymdesk ($75/mo with Gymdesk Payments, website included). {{aff:gymdesk|See Gymdesk pricing}}
  • New school that wants hands-on setup: Spark ($199/mo after an 8-week trial; an account rep handles setup and student data migration is free) or Zen Planner ($99/mo; free onboarding sessions with an onboarding coach). {{aff:zenplanner|See Zen Planner pricing}}

faq: What is the cheapest software for a new martial arts school?

Two tools publish a $0 start: MatPilot Free ($0/mo plus a 2% platform fee and Stripe's fee) and RhinoFit Start Up ($0/mo for 20 or fewer active users and $2,500 or less in monthly payments in the US and Canada; some features may be restricted). Among paid plans, MatGoat Basic is $40/mo for up to 50 students (matpilot.io, rhinofit.ca, matgoat.com pricing pages, checked 2026-11-18).
Can I use RhinoFit's free plan when my school starts?

Only while you have 20 or fewer active users and log or process $2,500 or less in payments a month (US and Canada). RhinoFit says Start Up users may have restricted or no access to communications and payment processing. Standard is $57/mo with no member limits (rhinofit.ca/pricing, checked 2026-11-18).
How early should I set up software before opening?

Zen Planner's pricing FAQ recommends having its system ready 3-6 months before launch. Most other tools offer a 7- to 30-day trial (Spark's is 8 weeks), so start the trial when you're ready to build your schedule, memberships and waiver.
Which school software has no contract?

Gymdesk (no contracts, $0 setup or cancellation), MatPilot, MatGoat, Martialytics, RhinoFit and MAAT's monthly plan say they're month to month or have no contract. Zen Planner is month to month with annual on request. Spark's term is set in your Order Form and auto-renews unless you give 30 days' notice (vendor pricing pages and Spark's Terms, checked 2026-11-18).
Does the price go up as my school grows?

With student-based pricing, yes: Kicksite goes from $49 to $99/mo at 26 students, Zen Planner from $99 to $133/mo at 46 active members, and Martialytics from $69 to $99/mo at 51. MatPilot Pro ($79/mo), MAAT ($59/mo), MatGoat Professional ($60/mo), RhinoFit Standard ($57/mo) and PushPress plans are flat with unlimited members.
